All three technologies (ceiling-mounted FMCW radar, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi sensing) are evaluated with the same convolutional neural network (CNN) on two tasks: fine-grained 10-class human activity recognition (HAR) and coarse 4-class sleep monitoring.
AI.result: IR-UWB achieved the highest cross-subject activity recognition performance (89.0% macro F1), while FMCW generalized best to unseen room layouts (83.8% macro F1). For sleep monitoring, all technologies exceeded 92% macro F1 in unseen environments. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off between recognition performance and environmental robustness, explained by differences in range resolution, antenna diversity, Doppler resolution, and spatial information retention.
AI.conclusion: The study provides practical guidelines for designing healthcare-oriented RF sensing systems, highlighting that different technologies have complementary strengths: IR-UWB excels at detailed activity recognition while FMCW offers better environmental robustness. All technologies perform well for sleep monitoring, making them suitable for different healthcare monitoring scenarios based on specific requirements.

title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
summary: Travel behavior research increasingly combines digital data collection with predictive modeling, yet these stages are often developed and evaluated separately. This study proposes a three-agent workflow integrating conversational data collection, structured data processing, and behavioral prediction. A chatbot-administered, image-augmented stated-preference survey collected mode choices from student commuters across five predefined weather scenarios, yielding 454 respondent-scenario observations. Weather-related associations were analyzed using a multinomial logit model, while logistic regression and random forest provided machine-learning benchmarks. Nine locally deployed large language models (LLMs), ranging from 2 to 35 billion parameters, were evaluated across four zero-shot prompt-and-context conditions and extended through persona, few-shot, and vision-based configurations. Random forest achieved 69.6% five-class accuracy, while the best text-only zero-shot LLM reached 69.9% without task-specific fitting. Habitual travel information produced the most consistent gains, Expert framing generally outperformed Role-Play, and persona information was most useful when habitual travel information was unavailable. Few-shot prompting improved prediction for several models, with gains stabilizing after a small number of examples. Using the same weather images shown to respondents, the best vision-based configuration reached 71.5% five-class accuracy, indicating that visual context may provide additional predictive information for selected models. Overall, the study shows how conversational surveys, structured data processing, conventional behavioral modeling, machine learning, and multimodal LLM prediction can be coordinated within an auditable multi-agent workflow.

AI.tldr: A three-agent workflow integrates conversational surveys, data processing, and behavioral prediction using LLMs and traditional models to predict mode choice under weather scenarios.
AI.motivation: Travel behavior research typically separates data collection and predictive modeling stages, limiting integrated analysis. The study aims to bridge this gap by developing a cohesive workflow that combines conversational data collection with multimodal predictive modeling.
AI.method: A chatbot-administered image-augmented stated-preference survey collected mode choices from student commuters across five weather scenarios. Used multinomial logit, logistic regression, random forest, and evaluated nine LLMs (2-35B parameters) with various prompting strategies including zero-shot, persona, few-shot, and vision-based configurations.
AI.result: Random forest achieved 69.6% accuracy, best text-only zero-shot LLM reached 69.9%. Habitual travel information was most predictive. Vision-based LLM configuration reached 71.5% accuracy using weather images shown to respondents. Few-shot prompting improved predictions with diminishing returns.
AI.conclusion: Conversational surveys, structured data processing, conventional modeling, machine learning, and multimodal LLM prediction can be effectively coordinated within an auditable multi-agent workflow, with LLMs showing competitive predictive performance without task-specific training.
